title: Concerning the Wheel and the Conduits
text:
⟨p.125⟩
ⲙⲫ
ⲙⲫ Concerning {1} {2}
The disciples questioned him, saying: 'Indeed, our Lord, con-
-cerning this also: How does the Wheel turn upon the heavens
which are stretched out from the winds to the earth — and yet they have not pierced them; or how
is it that the heavens do not mingle inward with the Wheel
as it turns and as it courses {3} {4}
The Illuminator answered them this: 'The heavens do not cleave (anything),
they cause no cleaving, since they are spiritual. Thus is
this, in which the heavens are likened to lions, in which the ships
are firmly fixed within them. For habitually the figurehead which is set at the head,
at the front of the ship, cleaves the lions, casting them
to this side and to that, every hour separating the lions
of that ship, opening to those (lions) at his place which is {8}
{9} at that very hour, before delay comes, the
lions are joined with one another upon their head of the ship, and the
path of the ship reveals itself in the midst of the lions.
As a bird that ascends out from the air, and his
path does not reveal itself in the air — in the manner of the men
in the sun: within the heavens, they do not mingle inward
with them, neither do they cut their path to be recognized out from the air.
Thus likewise is this of the Wheel: it turns within the heavens and
the air; the Wheel does not cleave the heavens, nor do they (the heavens) them-
{11}, the heavens, mingle inward with the Wheel.
